summary.intent: Stop the DatePicker showing the day before the chosen one for users east of UTC (issue 9129), and add integration tests for the widget.
summary.issue_fit: Partial — the post-selection display is fixed for UTC+ zones, but the initial value and min/max bounds that Python sends as UTC-midnight timestamps now display a day early for users west of UTC, where the base code was correct.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed; behavior of the old and new `_unlocal_date` traced and run in node across nine TZ values; Selenium tests not run (unavailable), settled by trace. Untracked `.mcp.json` in the clone is outside the range.
check_details: Reviewer-executed at head 36549bca: scratch node script comparing base and head `_unlocal_date` under TZ=UTC, Europe/Paris, Europe/London, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Auckland, America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, America/Sao_Paulo, Pacific/Honolulu; all exit 0 (see finding).
Unavailable: Selenium integration suite `tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py`, browser and project build are not available offline; the tests were read and traced, not run.

findings.title: Fix initial DatePicker day shifted back west of UTC
findings.trigger: Python sends `DatePicker(value=datetime.date(2019, 9, 20))`, `min_date` and `max_date` as UTC-midnight milliseconds, and `render()` passes them through `_unlocal_date`, which now subtracts `getTimezoneOffset()` before reading the UTC date; under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` a node run returns 2019-9-19 where the base returned 2019-9-20.
findings.impact: Every user west of UTC sees the initial input text and highlighted day one day early, and a `max_date` day becomes unselectable, a regression from the base code, which was only wrong east of UTC.
findings.change: In `_unlocal_date`, treat a numeric UTC-midnight timestamp with `new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate())` and the `toDateString()` string that `_on_select` stores with `new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())`, instead of one offset shift for both.

findings.title: Assert the initial displayed date in the DatePicker test
findings.trigger: `test_js_on_change_executes` clicks day 16 and reads the input text but never reads it before the click, and nothing sets the browser time zone.
findings.impact: The initial-display regression above passes unnoticed, and on a UTC runner the post-click assertion passes with the base `_unlocal_date` as well, so the test does not guard issue 9129.
findings.change: Before the first click, assert that `.foo input` has value `'Fri Sep 20 2019'`, and run the browser under a fixed non-UTC time zone so the assertion is sensitive to the offset.
findings.source: Issue 9129 (displayed value must match the chosen date).

observations.fact: `_unlocal_date` now mutates its `Date` argument through `setTime`, but every caller passes a freshly constructed `Date`, so nothing observes it.

requirements.evidence: With `_on_select` storing a `toDateString()` value, head `_unlocal_date` returns the chosen day in Paris, London, Kolkata and Auckland where the base returned the day before (node TZ matrix, `bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:78-88`).

`DatePicker(value=datetime.date.today())` is sent as UTC-midnight ms (`bokeh/util/serialization.py:183-184`); head shows it a day early under America/Los_Angeles, New_York, Sao_Paulo and Honolulu, while the base showed it correctly.
Title promises the UTC+ display fix, which the head delivers for the post-selection path (node TZ matrix).
The PST check ('working great') does not extend to the initial value: head returns 2019-9-19 for a UTC-midnight 2019-9-20 under America/Los_Angeles.
